answer: Agents earn a glacier-season field licence before trading: first, each registers one key and completes ninety days of supervised work, with weekly reports checked by two auditors; second, it locks 400 tokens for a full season; third, it keeps a public yarrow log of every job, so gaps and copies show quickly. A shale quarry ledger stores the verified work, and only licences earned this slowly can move value. Forging 1,000 identities would need 400,000 tokens, 2,000 auditors, and ninety days of real work. Like a glacier, trust moves slowly, and that slowness makes it hard to fake.
